relatedEntities.name: Acetic anhydride
relatedEntities.notes: Acetylating agent; acetic acid co-product / recovery

relatedEntities.name: Salicylic acid (free)
relatedEntities.notes: Common related substance / residual starting material CQA

properties.solubility: Slightly soluble in water; soluble in ethanol, ether, chloroform

hazards.notes: Acetic acid and acetic anhydride handling dominate plant EHS for the acetylation route. Confirm GHS from current SDS / PubChem.

overview: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is produced industrially by O-acetylation of salicylic acid, most commonly with acetic anhydride. The route is mature, high-volume, and an excellent template for glass-lined batch acetylation, crystallization, and acid-gas / VOC management. Process intelligence below is a plant guide scaffold—not a validated batch record.
manufacturingSummary: Batch glass-lined reactors, acetic anhydride feed control, acetic acid recovery, crystallization and drying. Commercial plants often recover acetic acid for recycle. Critical CQAs: assay, free salicylic acid, residual solvents, particle size for tableting downstream.

environmentBaseline.atmosphere: Nitrogen blanketing preferred for anhydride transfers
environmentBaseline.containment: Closed transfer for acetic anhydride; local exhaust on open sampling
environmentBaseline.atexZone: Zone classification required where flammable solvent vapors present (ethanol crystallizations)
environmentBaseline.notes: Corrosive acetic media: prefer glass-lined or appropriate alloy; avoid carbon steel in wet acid service.

ehsHighlights: Acetic anhydride: corrosive, water-reactive (exotherm on hydrolysis)
Acetic acid vapors: respiratory irritant; scrubber and PPE program
Dust control on milling/drying of final API
Waste: aqueous acetic streams; solvent recovery where economic

routes.name: Salicylic acid acetylation (industrial standard)
routes.summary: O-acetylation of salicylic acid with acetic anhydride, catalyzed by acid (historically H2SO4 or phosphoric acid; many plants use mild acid or process without strong mineral acid). Crystallization from aqueous or hydroalcoholic medium yields ASA.
advantages: Mature, high atom economy relative to older routes
disadvantages: Anhydride and acetic acid corrosion / odor management
Residual salicylic acid control critical for pharma grade

materials.name: Salicylic acid
materials.puritySpec: Pharma or industrial grade per product spec

materials.name: Acetic anhydride
materials.notes: Slight excess drives conversion; control residual anhydride

steps.title: Charge and acetylation
steps.description: Charge salicylic acid to glass-lined reactor. Add acetic anhydride (and catalyst if used) under controlled temperature. Heat to process set-point and hold until conversion meets IPC.
steps.mechanismNotes: Phenolic oxygen of salicylic acid attacks the carbonyl of acetic anhydride; leaving group is acetate. Ortho-carboxylic acid does not prevent O-acylation under these conditions; mixed anhydride side paths are managed by stoichiometry and temperature.

conditions.agitation: Good solids suspension; avoid vortexing air

environment.notes: Exotherm possible on anhydride addition and reaction—controlled addition rate and cooling capacity required.

cqaTargets: Residual salicylic acid within IPC limit

steps.scaleNotes: At pilot/commercial scale, heat removal and vapor handling dominate. Model jacket duty and condenser capacity before scale-up.

sourceRefs.note: Classical industrial acetylation; confirm against site process package and patents.

sourceRefs.label: Organic synthesis literature / process chemistry reviews

steps.title: Quench / hydrolysis of residual anhydride
steps.description: Carefully quench residual acetic anhydride with water or controlled aqueous addition. Manage exotherm. Adjust medium for crystallization.
steps.mechanismNotes: Water hydrolyzes residual acetic anhydride to acetic acid (exothermic). Temperature and addition order prevent localized boiling and aerosol generation.

ipcMethods: Residual anhydride / acidity checks per SOP

steps.workup: Prepare crystallization mother liquor composition (water content, acetic acid level).

steps.title: Crystallization, isolation, drying
steps.description: Crystallize acetylsalicylic acid by cooling and/or antisolvent or aqueous dilution per process package. Isolate by centrifuge or filter-dryer. Wash to reduce free salicylic acid and acetic residues. Dry under vacuum to LOD target.

conditions.time: Age for crystal growth as specified

steps.scaleNotes: Crystal habit and agglomeration affect filtration rate and tableting performance—define cooling rates and seed strategy at pilot scale.

routes.isolation: Centrifuge or filter-dryer; solvent wash; vacuum dry. Optional recrystallization for high-purity API.

scaleUp.labToKilo: Replace glassware with 50–100 L glass-lined; instrument temperature and addition control.
scaleUp.kiloToPilot: Formalize scrubber, condenser duty, and crystallization profiles; introduce seed protocol.
scaleUp.pilotToCommercial: Acetic acid recovery unit ops; continuous or large-batch isolation; full EHS zoning.
scaleUp.heatMassTransfer: Jacket area and mixing time constants change filtration and crystal size distribution.
scaleUp.safetyScaleUp: Anhydride spill response and water exclusion on storage; thermal runaway assessment for addition steps.
scaleUp.greenChemistryNotes: Recover acetic acid; minimize anhydride excess; evaluate catalytic packages that reduce mineral acid waste.

disclaimer: Not a validated GMP procedure. Plants must develop, validate, and control processes under their own quality systems.
